subject: released breedR v0.12 with basic multitrait support

messages.author: 37c4b6bc71d5d203
messages.subject: released breedR v0.12 with basic multitrait support
parts:
Dear breedRs,

I have the pleasure to announce this long awaited feature: breedR now
has a basic support for multitrait models.

It is "/basic/" because there are no options to fine-control the
covariance structures: all random effects will have a full covariance
matrix estimated with dimensions equal to the number of traits.

The bright side of it is that the interface is *really* simple. Models
are specified exactly in the same way, with the only exception of the
response variable in the `fixed` formula.

Go ahead and try it out:

|packageVersion("breedR") #> [1] '0.12' res <- remlf90( fixed =
cbind(LAS, DOS) ~ rep, random = ~ bl, genetic = list( model =
'add_animal', pedigree = larix[, 1:3], id = 'self' ), data = larix) #>
Using default initial variances given by default_initial_variance() #>
See ?breedR.getOption. summary(res) #> Formula: cbind(LAS, DOS) ~ 0 +
rep + bl + pedigree #> Data: larix #> AIC BIC logLik #> 67577 67666
-33777 #> #> Parameters of special components: #> #> #> Variance
components: #> Estimated variances S.E. #> bl.LAS 0.008121 0.009891 #>
bl.LAS_bl.DOS -0.004856 0.004975 #> bl.DOS 0.005324 0.004505 #>
genetic.direct.LAS 0.056213 0.018434 #>
genetic.direct.LAS_genetic.direct.DOS -0.094390 0.022805 #>
genetic.direct.DOS 0.378640 0.024296 #> Residual.LAS 8.328000 0.108590
#> Residual.LAS_Residual.DOS -0.247570 0.022419 #> Residual.DOS 0.675550
0.009063 #> #> Estimate S.E. #> Heritability:LAS 0.00668 0.002161 #>
Heritability:DOS 0.35727 0.015504 #> #> Fixed effects: #> value s.e. #>
rep.LAS.1 6.16367 0.0989 #> rep.LAS.2 6.00958 0.0972 #> rep.LAS.3
6.20569 0.0996 #> rep.LAS.4 5.90350 0.1015 #> rep.LAS.5 6.33785 0.1064
#> rep.LAS.6 6.30413 0.1021 #> rep.LAS.7 6.08759 0.1023 #> rep.LAS.8
5.98522 0.1018 #> rep.DOS.1 0.42089 0.1383 #> rep.DOS.2 0.36545 0.1375
#> rep.DOS.3 0.32589 0.1379 #> rep.DOS.4 0.43896 0.1388 #> rep.DOS.5
0.26516 0.1404 #> rep.DOS.6 0.20119 0.1391 #> rep.DOS.7 0.33567 0.1389
#> rep.DOS.8 0.43656 0.1392|

Admittedly, I have not conducted thorough testing as I wanted to release
as soon as possible. I count on you to report issues you might find, and
help me polish the tool.

The change is important enough to merit a minor version bump (we jumped
from v0.11-5 to v0.12).

This version should be __*mostly*__ backwards compatible. You might
notice some differences in the outcome of functions `fixef()` and
`fitted()` that can break some of your existing code. But it shouldn't
be difficult to figure out. These changes were necessary for a more
consistent and general outcome structure.

Good testing. And please let me know of any problems you might have,
either here of filing an issue <https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/issues>.

Thank you in advance!

ƒacu.-


--

messages.subject: Re: released breedR v0.12 with basic multitrait support
parts:
Dear all,

the first important issue has been detected (thanks to Vincent Segura) and fixed in a new version 0.12-1 which has just been deployed.

While in my last e-mail I said that there are no options to control de cross-covariance structure of specific effects, this is not entirely true. In fact, by setting some initial covariances to 0 you can prevent this particular component to be estimated and reduce in this way the dimension of the model. So, you can define models without spatial or residual cross-covariances (think multi-site, for example).

The bug had to do with recovering results from this “reduced dimension” use case, under AI-REML, and is now fixed.

In addition, I wrote a short section in breedR’s “Overview” vignette [1] for multi-trait models.

Go ahead, and update.packages(oldPkgs = "breedR")

All the best,

ƒacu.-

[1] https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/wiki/Overview#multiple-traits

El 13/04/2017 a las 13:53, Facundo Muñoz escribió:

Dear breedRs,

I have the pleasure to announce this long awaited feature: breedR now
has a basic support for multitrait models.

It is "/basic/" because there are no options to fine-control the
covariance structures: all random effects will have a full covariance
matrix estimated with dimensions equal to the number of traits.

The bright side of it is that the interface is *really* simple. Models
are specified exactly in the same way, with the only exception of the
response variable in the `fixed` formula.

Go ahead and try it out:

|packageVersion("breedR") #> [1] '0.12' res <- remlf90( fixed =
cbind(LAS, DOS) ~ rep, random = ~ bl, genetic = list( model =
'add_animal', pedigree = larix[, 1:3], id = 'self' ), data = larix) #>
Using default initial variances given by default_initial_variance() #>
See ?breedR.getOption. summary(res) #> Formula: cbind(LAS, DOS) ~ 0 +
rep + bl + pedigree #> Data: larix #> AIC BIC logLik #> 67577 67666
-33777 #> #> Parameters of special components: #> #> #> Variance
components: #> Estimated variances S.E. #> bl.LAS 0.008121 0.009891 #>
bl.LAS_bl.DOS -0.004856 0.004975 #> bl.DOS 0.005324 0.004505 #>
genetic.direct.LAS 0.056213 0.018434 #>
genetic.direct.LAS_genetic.direct.DOS -0.094390 0.022805 #>
genetic.direct.DOS 0.378640 0.024296 #> Residual.LAS 8.328000 0.108590
#> Residual.LAS_Residual.DOS -0.247570 0.022419 #> Residual.DOS 0.675550
0.009063 #> #> Estimate S.E. #> Heritability:LAS 0.00668 0.002161 #>
Heritability:DOS 0.35727 0.015504 #> #> Fixed effects: #> value s.e. #>
rep.LAS.1 6.16367 0.0989 #> rep.LAS.2 6.00958 0.0972 #> rep.LAS.3
6.20569 0.0996 #> rep.LAS.4 5.90350 0.1015 #> rep.LAS.5 6.33785 0.1064
#> rep.LAS.6 6.30413 0.1021 #> rep.LAS.7 6.08759 0.1023 #> rep.LAS.8
5.98522 0.1018 #> rep.DOS.1 0.42089 0.1383 #> rep.DOS.2 0.36545 0.1375
#> rep.DOS.3 0.32589 0.1379 #> rep.DOS.4 0.43896 0.1388 #> rep.DOS.5
0.26516 0.1404 #> rep.DOS.6 0.20119 0.1391 #> rep.DOS.7 0.33567 0.1389
#> rep.DOS.8 0.43656 0.1392|

Admittedly, I have not conducted thorough testing as I wanted to release
as soon as possible. I count on you to report issues you might find, and
help me polish the tool.

The change is important enough to merit a minor version bump (we jumped
from v0.11-5 to v0.12).

This version should be __*mostly*__ backwards compatible. You might
notice some differences in the outcome of functions `fixef()` and
`fitted()` that can break some of your existing code. But it shouldn't
be difficult to figure out. These changes were necessary for a more
consistent and general outcome structure.

Good testing. And please let me know of any problems you might have,
either here of filing an issue <https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/issues>.

Thank you in advance!

        ƒacu.-

messages.author: 4481f1b251a490d4
messages.subject: Re: released breedR v0.12 with basic multitrait support
parts:
Facundo,
This is a great news, thank you so much.
I ran sevreal tests on my own data (with method = 'em') and compared the results with those of packages I usually use (espicially VCE and WOMBAT) to fit multivariate animal models .
I'm very happy to report that the results of a multitrait animal model (tested up to a 6 traits model) are comparable (practically the same) between breedr and these packages.
Finally we've an R package capable of fitting multitraits animal models with an easy to use interface.
Now, the challange is to come up with an equally easy to use interface to fit different models for different traits in breedr (Check out the Rdmu package written by the authors of the DMU package).

Best regards,

Nabeel.

Thank you for your comments Nabeel.

Indeed, trait-wise models are a natural extension which is already designed to a certain extent.

What is lacking is developer time. I expect to continue working in these and other missing functionalities in my free time, since the project has formally finished. But that would be slow in the best scenario. Ideally, someone will take over with money from other projects or whatever. I will be happy to help in that case.

ƒacu.-
